narrative.overview:
Butwal Hacks is a workshop, not a showroom. The design feels raw, honest, and maker-focused — red as a functional tool, glass as the workbench surface. Every pixel serves the builder: clear hierarchy, tactile buttons, surfaces that feel solid without calling attention to themselves. This is a space for getting things done, not for decoration.

The system rejects dark-mode-with-purple-gradients SaaS clichés, generic AI-tool marketing gloss, and anything that looks like a 2014 startup landing page. Instead, it builds depth from *material honesty*: liquid glass surfaces that feel substantial through blur and saturation rather than drop shadows, and a single assertive red accent that earns its place by being used sparingly.
keyCharacteristics: Honest materiality — glass surfaces (backdrop-blur-[30px] saturate-[180%]) replace empty shadows as the primary depth signal
Single accent discipline — Hackathon Red (#FE0000) is the only accent. It appears on ≤ 10% of any screen. Its rarity is the point.
Tool-like buttons — pill-shaped (rounded-full), substantial padding, spring-loaded hover scale (scale-[1.02] / scale-[1.03]), active press (scale-[0.97])
Mono confidence — JetBrains Mono for labels, badges, and metadata signals 'this is technical, this is precise'
Dark-first — Deep Space (#242424) is the default canvas. Starlight surfaces emerge as needed. Light mode exists but is secondary.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Hackathon Red is the only accent color. Status colors exist for signal, not for decoration. If more than one red-based element appears in a single viewport, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Hackathon Red occupies ≤ 10% of any screen. Its infrequency is what makes it meaningful. If elements are fighting for red, the hierarchy is broken.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: If it needs to communicate technical precision (a badge, a trust level, a cryptographic signature, a keyboard shortcut, an ID), it's in JetBrains Mono uppercase. If it's a paragraph or headline, it's DM Sans. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus). If a card has a shadow at rest, it's either a modal or it's wrong.

rules.name: The Glass-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: When both glass and shadow could work, choose glass. backdrop-blur creates material depth; shadows create visual noise.

dos: Do use lg-surface (or GlassPrimitive variant="default") as the primary container pattern for all card-like sections
Do use rounded-full for all buttons, badges, and interactive pills
Do reserve Hackathon Red (#FE0000) exclusively for CTAs, trust markers, and verified badges — never for decorative borders or gratuitous accents
Do use JetBrains Mono uppercase for all badges, labels, timestamps, and metadata
Do apply the spring transition (duration-[400ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275)]) to interactive elements
Do use focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-primary-red/50 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-bg-base rounded-lg as the global focus indicator
Do prefer backdrop-blur + saturate over box-shadow for creating surface depth
Do use glass surfaces (translucent) for containers and solid surfaces (bg-surface) for dense information displays
Do use the custom-scrollbar utility (scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--bh-border) transparent) for scrollable sections
donts: Don't use inline style={{}} for colors — always use Tailwind arbitrary values (bg-[#FE0000], text-[#242424])
Don't apply box shadows to cards at rest — surfaces should appear flat until hovered
Don't use more than one accent color on a single screen. The red IS the accent. Status colors are signal, not decoration.
Don't use purple gradients, neon accents, or glassmorphism with saturated rainbow backdrops (anti-reference: generic SaaS landing page)
Don't animate elements on page load unless they convey meaningful information (anti-reference: animated header counters that exist purely for visual effect)
Don't use DM Sans for metadata or badges — that's what JetBrains Mono is for
Don't mix glass and solid card styles in the same section — pick one container language per layout zone
Don't apply the lg-surface pattern to navigation or top-level structural elements — use solid bg-surface for sidebars and nav bars
Don't create new color tokens outside the palette without a documented reason. If you need a new shade, derive it from the existing scale.
